event: Wren wakes in the dark because the compass is pulling SSW, insistent.
The Shelf is there too, cold with the small-hours chill of exposed limestone.
Day 3. The insect chorus still runs: dry, and earlier than the thrush.
She laces her boots in the dark and takes only compass, journal, tin cup and sage.
She does not wake Theron; she is afraid she would obey his question.
She goes, by the landmarks she sketched yesterday.
At night the whole upper basin holds the ghost-elm hum like a chord.
She crosses the fen margin in the dark on the root-firm ground Hadley taught her.
The Shelf brightens in her chest as she nears the Eye: bonds sense bond-potentials.
At night the Warden's Eye is a mirror, showing stars she cannot see overhead.
[Wayfinder's Eye] focuses deeper than yesterday, as if the pool has been waiting.
She puts her bare feet in the water; it registers as attention, not temperature.
She sets her palms in the water and reaches with her Sympathetic extension.
The pool reaches back: two threads of attention wind together like fingers.
She trembles: palm to palm through glass, two living things recognizing each other.
The bond seals; light from the depths pulses three times and settles to a glow.
She feels the Eye in her: clarity and depth, beside the Shelf's cool stone.
SYMPATHETIC BOND FORMED: Warden's Eye, Glimpsed, [Reflective], Reciprocal, +50 XP.

changes.note: Sympathetic Bond formed: Warden's Eye, Reciprocal

event: Reciprocal bonds form when a place takes part; she reads the word three times.
She understands the pool has been paying attention for a very long time.
Dawn softens the mirror; she feels the Eye's night-watch ease into dawn-patience.
Places have rhythms, she files, as people have moods.
She walks back to camp in early light carrying two places in her chest.
Theron is at the fire, looking south-east; he looks at her damp boots.
'The fen.' 'The pool.' 'You bonded it.' 'It bonded me back.'
His grandmother told of the Eye choosing; it had not done so in her lifetime.
Through EMP 10 Wren feels what he does not say: the Rimfolk scattered after the pool.
She says she left before dawn and should have told him. 'You should have.'
She followed every landmark; she felt the pool was waiting.
'My grandmother would have liked you,' Theron says, and tends the fire.
Hadley comes out at the smell of flatcakes, soil fresh on his hands.
'Your face is doing a thing.' She tells him she bonded the Warden's Eye.
The compass woke her, she explains; it pulled hard enough to feel in her sleep.
'Reciprocal,' she says, and Hadley is struck silent for three full seconds.
He asks her to show him what seeing with two places looks like.
After breakfast they go south to the mid-canopy for silvervein moss.
The second bond is not a doubling but a deepening: the Shelf grounds, the Eye sharpens.
At a cluster of three ghost elms she feels their hums overlap into one resonance.
Hadley presses his palm beside hers and feels a tingling.
The air smells of ozone and old wood; the grove's edges blur with vibration.
The trees are responding to something underground, and not dying: resisting.
At the grove's edge a band of held-empty soil: the corruption cannot cross the resonance.
Hadley finds finer soil inside; in three seasons he has never seen this.
'I think the Thornwild isn't just sick. I think it's fighting back.'
A discovery: ghost-elm groves are the Thornwild's immune response, +65 XP.

changes.note: Discovery: ghost-elm resonance network resists corruption

event: She shows him moss grown toward the other trees and a root that turned back.
Hadley takes real notes, murmuring 'yes, yes' at every point.
Walking back north, the Shelf brightens in her chest.
Through the Eye she feels the Shelf: its stone cooling, a cold high wind bending the rowan.
'I'm in two places at once,' she whispers; the bonds talk through her.
BOND NETWORK DETECTED: two nodes, Nascent, +80 XP for a first network.

changes.note: First: bond network formed between Shelf and Eye

event: Connections grow geometrically; a Wayfinder weaves places together.
She sits down against a ghost elm, the hum in her spine.
North-east of the grove the compass erupts with dozens of competing pulls.
She staggers; Hadley catches her arm. 'Bond-potentials. Too many. All at once.'
In ten breaths she learns to hear them apart; all point north-east, close.
Hadley wants to go back, then closes his notebook: 'All right. Show me.'
They push through thorny young growth into a stretch of disrupted canopy.
Her foot hits a straight line in the earth: cut stone, a mason's groove.
It turns a perfect right angle: a wall corner, a building.
Hadley knows it: Rimfolk stonework, with a Rimfolk guild mark.
She feels a whole settlement under the green, still here.
The worked stone is warm, as if remembering the hands that shaped it.
The compass settles from cacophony into one coherent, waiting hum.
SIGNIFICANT DISCOVERY: unnamed settlement ruins, 15+ bond-potentials, +150 XP.

changes.note: Discovery: settlement ruins (+120) and first cluster detection (+30)

event: Surveying activates; the System recommends a systematic survey.
That evening Wren tells Theron of the bond network, wonder in her voice.
Of the groves he says his father knew they were healthier, and never why.
She keeps the ruins to herself for one night; she will tell him in the morning.
In her bedroll she feels the two bonds like a heart with two chambers.
Beyond them, north-east, the ruins hum faintly, dreaming under green.
Every trunk seems to exhale at once, a sound at the edge of hearing like weeping.
The Crying Forest's next event is fifteen days away.
The forest isn't grieving, she thinks; it is remembering.
She sleeps carrying three places: stone, water, and one she has not yet touched.
